transcript:
This message comes from Schwab. At Schwab, you can get everything from self-directed investing to full-service wealth management, all in one place.
No matter your investing goal, life stage, amount to invest, or know-how, you can invest your way with Schwab.
President Trump is going to Nebraska today to campaign for Republican Senator Pete Ricketts. The GOP incumbent is facing a strong challenge from independent candidate Dan Osborn, who is backed by national Democrats.
Vice President Vance is going to Fairbanks, Alaska today to support GOP candidates. The Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee is throwing its support behind six additional candidates ahead of the midterm elections.
As NPR's Tamara Keith reports, the six candidates are running in districts where Republicans have an edge.
The committee's red to blue is its top-tier backing for candidates and comes with staff resources and fundraising support.
All six candidates newly added to the list face challenging races. Only one is in a district rated by the Cook Political Report as lean Republican. The others face even longer odds.
For instance, Nevada's second congressional district, where candidate Teresa Benitez-Thompson, earned the red to blue nod. That district has not elected a Democrat since its creation in the early 1980s.
A spokesman for the National Republican Congressional Committee said describing that race as competitive is delusional. Tamara Keith, NPR News.
Saudi-backed Yemeni forces say they have launched an operation to recapture Western territory from Iran-backed Houthi fighters.
NPR's Aya Batrawi reports the Houthis are capturing more territory in Yemen and call the offensive "wishful thinking."
The Saudi Air Force and Yemeni government forces are targeting Houthi fighters across Yemen with fighter jets and missiles, including in the Houthi-controlled capital of Sana'a.
The Houthis, meanwhile, are launching drones and missiles at Saudi Arabia. The Iran-backed group says they hit two Aramco oil sites in recent days, including one in the Saudi capital, Riyadh. Saudi Arabia has not commented.
The fiercest fighting, however, is taking place in the southwestern Yemeni province of Taz, where the Houthis captured a key port city and territory along the Red Sea last month.
The Associated Press reports the Houthis on Sunday advanced in Taz, capturing the town of Torba. This potentially cuts off a key road linking the provincial city of Taz from the de facto Yemeni government capital of Aden in the far south.
Aya Batrawi, NPR News, Dubai.
The investigation into last week's attack on a passenger jet headed to Tel Aviv finds that the co-pilot intended to crash the jet into Israel's Ben Gurion airport.
That's according to a person familiar with the matter, but not authorized to speak publicly.
Spanish voters will go to the polls later this year to elect a new parliament. That's after Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez announced snap elections this morning.
As NPR's Miguel Macias reports from Seville, the decision was expected after an eventful week in Spanish politics.
Speaking from the presidential palace, Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez went over the achievements of his coalition government, from his stance on the wars in the Middle East to domestic legislation on social and economic issues.
That track record, Sanchez says, has turned Spain into a world reference of "peace, feminism and prosperity".
Borders will go to the polls on Sunday, November 29th.
The latest polls give a hypothetical coalition of right-leaning parties and majority in Congress.
But Sanchez is hoping to ride a wave of discontent over a national housing crisis that for the past two weeks have resulted in protests across the country
and fighting over proposed emergency legislation to address that crisis. Miguel Macias, NPR News, Seville, Spain.
The Pentagon says that it has brought home all of its military bomber planes that were stationed at an airbase in the United Kingdom.
This is the same base where British authorities arrested five men who are suspected of plotting to attack that airbase.
I'm Corva Coleman, NPR News in Washington.
Amazon Prime members can listen to NPR News now, sponsor free through Amazon Music.
Or you can also support NPR's vital journalism and get NPR+ at plus.npr.org. That's plus.npr.org.

Vice President Vance travels to Fairbanks, Alaska to support GOP candidates
Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee backs six additional candidates in challenging midterm races
Saudi-backed Yemeni forces launch operation to recapture western territory from Iran-backed Houthis
Houthi fighters capture town of Torba in southwestern Yemen, potentially cutting key road
Investigation finds co-pilot in attack on Tel Aviv-bound jet intended to crash into Ben Gurion
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez announces snap elections for November 29th parliament
